rows.caution: A reader should not treat the convergence of these two routes as independent corroboration that strengthens the causal claim. Route A is a small, thickness-confounded correlation across three conditions of possibly-uncontrolled orientation; Route B is a qualitative, unpaired plausibility argument that does not measure yield stress for the same microstructural states it describes, and in fact highlights an orientation effect large enough to be a rival explanation for Route A's pattern. Two weak, non-independent, differently-confounded associations do not sum to strong or mechanistic support -- the reader should not conclude that nanoplate density (as opposed to thickness, orientation, or other heat-treatment-induced changes) has been shown to cause the observed yield-stress differences, only that the idea remains plausible and unrefuted by either route.

A reader should not treat the two routes together as proving kink banding is the sole or dominant, quantitatively established mechanism for the ~45% tensile plastic strain -- neither route rules out concurrent contributions from other deformation modes (e.g. basal slip), and Route B explicitly cannot resolve which portion of the mechanical response maps to which microstructural event. Nor should the reader conclude that compression is intrinsically incapable of kink-band formation -- only that it fractures before any such route can manifest, per Route A's own limits. The routes' evidence is also not as independent as it first appears: Route A's 'kink bands' language borrows from the same microstructural fact (F10b/OM banding) that Route B directly evidences, so this is not two fully separate lines of proof converging, and combined they still amount only to a qualitative, single-condition ([0001], RT) association -- not strong, generalizable, or quantitative support.

A reader should not treat this as two independent lines of evidence converging on the claim, since the routes share the same core charge-transfer figures rather than being fully disjoint measurements -- so there is evidentiary overlap, not full triangulation. Neither route establishes that the effect is specific to pyridinic-N (both model generic N-doping/doped sites), so the reader should not conclude the pyridinic-to-graphitic nitrogen mechanism has been isolated. Route B alone cannot support any energetic/thermodynamic language, since it never touches adsorption energies; only Route A's additional data does that, and even Route A only claims consistency, not proof, with the specific experimental mechanism. Two routes that each only partly support the conclusion, and that partly overlap in evidence, should not be read as adding up to strong or discriminating support for a pyridinic-N-specific thermodynamic driving force.

A reader should not treat convergence of the two routes as independent triangulation that strengthens the causal conclusion. Both routes ultimately rest on the same limited electrochemical observation (a two-point plateau comparison, -0.05 V vs -0.10 V, at only the lowest and highest tested rates), and each route's 'extra' evidence (chemistry/DFT in A, SEM morphology in B) is linked to that observation only associatively, with explicit gaps in matching conditions or identifying shared sites/stages. Two routes that each only weakly and associatively support the conclusion, while sharing their core anchor data point, do not sum to strong or mechanistically demonstrated support -- they should be read as two plausible, mutually compatible narrative elaborations of the same underlying weak two-point measurement, not as convergent proof.

A reader should not treat two routes reaching the same headline conclusion as independent triangulation. They share a common empirical anchor (the same 91 mAh/g first-discharge value from panel F2a), so this is closer to one measurement described twice than two disjoint lines of evidence. Neither route confirms the dual V/Fe redox-couple mechanism, isolates crystallinity (or any single structural variable) as the cause of the capacity ordering, or validates the earlier-PBA benchmark comparison under matched conditions -- so the pair should not be read as upgrading a weak, cross-study/associative claim into a mechanistically or comparatively confirmed one.

A reader should not treat two independently-arriving, similarly-ranked routes as adding up to a validated causal or mechanistic account. Route A's association is confounded by synthesis route and limited to an ordinal, cross-type comparison with no dose-response or slope; Route B's association is confirmed by matched XRD+PL data only for PC (not HOC/SC), spans mismatched temperature windows, and explicitly lacks a demonstrated mechanism linking structural fraction to PL feature. Combining two associative, individually weak/partly-warranted routes does not compound into strong or discriminating evidence -- it remains descriptive/associative co-variation across three confounded samples, not a validated inverse relationship or causal mechanism.

A reader should not treat two hedged/limited routes as summing to a validated causal mechanism. Neither route confirms that the platelet/thrombosis assays occurred within the >8h sustained-release window, and neither disentangles the NO-specific effect from the BVLD confound present in the combined BVLD/NO-PPAmF surface — if anything Route B's inclusion of the BVLD-only surface sharpens that confound rather than removing it. The routes are also not fully independent evidence: Route B's paired series (platelet count and activation across the five surfaces) is drawn from essentially the same underlying obs2/obs3 measurements that Route A cites, so their agreement partly reflects shared source data rather than two truly separate corroborating lines. Two associative/hedged supports do not add up to strong mechanistic support; the conclusion remains a plausible, not established, mechanism.

A reader should not treat the two routes as independent lines of evidence that jointly upgrade a weak claim into a strong one. Both routes trace back to the same structural fact of the experiment -- that Co content, surface texture, and group identity all move together because they are set by one synthesis variable across only three scaffolds -- so they are correlated demonstrations of the same confound rather than independent tests that could have disagreed and didn't. Route A explicitly concludes cause cannot be separated, and Route B's own limits admit its match is largely a construction check; neither route rules out texture (or any other co-varying property) as the actual driver of release, and Route A's own attempt to do so is flagged as resting on a cross-kind, unverified comparison. Combining two routes that each only support an ordinal/associative relationship, and that share rather than diversify their key limitation, does not produce a discriminating or mechanistic conclusion -- it should still be read as 'composition and release are consistently ordered across a confounded design,' not as 'composition determines release.'

A reader should not treat the two routes together as building toward a demonstrated causal mechanism linking pore/texture structure to release kinetics. Route A's own limits show its inverse-order argument relies on surface-area numbers not actually verified in the cited data, so it should not be read as a settled ruling-out of texture as a cause -- only as flagging an unresolved confound. Route B's co-occurrence of structural order and gradual release should not be read as evidence that pores are the transport pathway, since no dose-response or matched-sample comparison was established. Two hedged, associative/confound-limited routes on disjoint evidence do not sum to strong or mechanistic support for claim n15; at most they show the claim is not contradicted by either dataset while remaining unestablished by both.

A reader should not treat 'two independent routes reaching the same conclusion' as doubling the evidential weight or as triangulation from independent data. Both routes ultimately rest on the same drug-free-vs-ampicillin-loaded survival comparison as their real evidence against Co2+-alone; the additional material in each (pore-structure/release-curve in A, HIF-1alpha Co-dose blot in B) is explicitly self-flagged in both routes as qualitative, unreplicated, and not measured against the antibacterial outcome. Neither route shows the effect is specific to 2Co-MBG (survival data are not broken out by composition in either), so the conclusion should be read as an association (ampicillin presence correlates with killing; Co2+ alone does not) rather than a calibrated dose-response or a mechanistically discriminating result, and the agreement between routes should not be read as strengthening that beyond what the shared survival data alone already supports.

A reader should not treat the two routes as independent confirmation that adds up to strong, mechanistic support for claim n13. Route B is purely associative/compatibility-level and is confounded by particle content, so it cannot be used to argue that dispersion morphology causally drives the YS trend that Route A also relies on for its YS side of the divergence claim. Route A itself does not establish a quantified magnitude comparison between YS gains and creep gains (different quantities, possibly different test temperatures, and a threshold-like rather than continuous pattern). Stacking a partly-warranted descriptive claim (A) with a weak associative, confounded claim (B) does not yield a strong composite argument -- the reader should not conclude that composition's differential effect on YS vs. creep is mechanistically explained by microstructural dispersion, since no route actually links dispersion morphology to creep behavior at all.

Having two routes reach the same conclusion should not be read as independent corroboration that resolves the confound or upgrades the finding to a causal or mechanistic claim: both routes are confounded by the same variable (Ag:Pd composition co-varies with whatever separation/photocurrent metric is used and with H2 evolution rate), both are limited to the same 4-sample overlap while ignoring 2 measured H2-evolution compositions, and both establish only rank-order matching rather than a quantitative, unit-comparable, or dose-response relationship. A reader should not conclude that photocarrier separation or photocurrent causes higher H2 evolution, should not extend the pattern to the untested compositions, and should not treat two associative, similarly-confounded routes as adding up to strong or mechanistic support -- they replicate one association via two downstream proxies rather than independently verifying it.

A reader should not treat two independently weak routes as summing to strong or mechanistic support. Neither route has data at the actual ZT peak temperature (500-525K) matched against its cited quantity (kappa or PF), so 'both routes point to x=0.01' is a coincidence of composition labels across different temperature ranges, not a demonstrated causal chain from low kappa_L+kappa_b and high power factor to the specific ZT peak magnitude. Neither route includes kappa_e, so the full ZT decomposition is never assembled in either route, let alone across both. And Route A's own 300K data (x=0.005 has the higher room-temperature ZT despite not being the lowest-kappa or highest-PF composition) is a real counter-signal that the combination does not explain away. The correct takeaway is a plausible, formula-consistent association for one composition at one loosely-defined temperature range -- not a validated mechanism, and not confirmation that the two independent (disjoint-evidence) analyses corroborate each other in a strong sense.

A reader should not treat having two routes as two independent lines of evidence that add up to stronger support. Both routes draw on the exact same underlying measurement (the same obs1 height-loss-vs-time curve, same numbers, same single time point, same qualitative jaggedness observation), so combining them does not increase the sample size, add a second independent metric, or supply a mechanism -- it is the same weak, single-timepoint, non-repeated directional observation cited twice under different framings. Neither route establishes a quantitative or causal link between wear rate and cumulative height loss (both explicitly deny this), and Route B openly states its own evidence is not an independent confirmation of the prior step's figure. Two weak, non-independent routes do not sum to strong support; at most they confirm that both backbone chains are being applied consistently to the same limited dataset, not that the underlying evidence for the conclusion has grown stronger.

A reader should not conclude that either route -- separately or combined -- identifies what causes the Na-side fade. Route A cannot isolate porosity/structure from ion-electrolyte/SEI confounds, and its cycle-40 figure mixes non-equivalent charge/discharge metrics, so it cannot support a quantitative degradation claim past cycle 1 on a strict like-for-like basis. Route B cannot show that the confirmed Co3O4/CoO phase mixture persists, changes, or is causally responsible for the fade, since XRD was taken only pre-cycling. Combining two associative, mechanism-blind routes does not create a mechanistic or discriminating account -- it only corroborates that the fade is real and severe, not why it occurs or whether porosity or phase composition is the operative variable.

A reader should not treat the two routes as fully independent triangulation, since both rely on the same EBSD orientation-map observation as one of their two evidentiary legs -- only the second leg differs (SAED vs. OM). The combination should not be read as establishing a quantified misorientation magnitude (SAED gives only four discrete angle readings on wavy bands, not a systematic profile, and was never applied to twin bands for comparison), nor as establishing a causal/mechanistic account of why kink bands show continuously varying orientation while twin bands do not (dislocation-mediated rotation vs. discrete twinning is implied by the pattern of observations but not demonstrated). The agreement of two partly-warranted routes that share a common evidentiary leg does not amount to strong, discriminating proof; it is best read as reinforcing correlational/associative support for the claim, not a validated mechanism.
